name: ALG11-CDG (congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ip)

clinicalPearls: ALG11 encodes the endoplasmic reticulum alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase that adds the fourth and fifth mannose residues, extending Man3GlcNAc2 to Man5GlcNAc2 on the cytosolic face of the ER.
The core phenotype is a severe infantile epileptic encephalopathy with profound developmental delay, central hypotonia and acquired (progressive) microcephaly.
Sensorineural hearing loss is a notably frequent feature and helps flag ALG11 among the type I CDGs.
Recurrent unexplained hyperthermia or fever episodes without an infective source are described.
Dysmorphic CDG stigmata such as inverted nipples and abnormal subcutaneous fat pads may be present.
Carbohydrate-deficient transferrin shows a type I pattern; fibroblast lipid-linked oligosaccharide analysis shows accumulation of the Man3-4GlcNAc2 species.
Neuroimaging typically demonstrates hypomyelination and cerebral atrophy.
reference.pathophysiology: ALG11-CDG is an autosomal recessive type I congenital disorder of glycosylation resulting from biallelic variants in ALG11, which encodes GDP-mannose:Man3GlcNAc2-PP-dolichol alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase. On the cytosolic face of the endoplasmic reticulum this enzyme transfers the fourth and fifth mannose residues onto the growing dolichol-linked oligosaccharide, extending Man3GlcNAc2 to Man5GlcNAc2 before the intermediate is flipped into the ER lumen for further elongation. Enzyme deficiency arrests this elongation, producing truncated lipid-linked oligosaccharides, reduced transfer of the complete glycan to protein and generalised hypoglycosylation; the developing central nervous system and cochlea appear especially vulnerable, accounting for the epileptic encephalopathy, developmental impairment and sensorineural deafness that characterise the disorder.
additionalDifferentials: ALG1-CDG (CDG-Ik), which adds the first mannose and causes a clinically similar severe encephalopathy
ALG2-CDG (CDG-Ii), the adjacent enzyme adding the second and third mannoses
PMM2-CDG (CDG-Ia), the prototypic type I CDG
Other genetic early-infantile epileptic encephalopathies unrelated to glycosylation
Mitochondrial encephalopathies presenting with epilepsy and sensorineural hearing loss
additionalInvestigations: Serum transferrin isoelectric focusing / carbohydrate-deficient transferrin (type I pattern)
Molecular genetic testing or exome sequencing for biallelic ALG11 variants
Lipid-linked oligosaccharide profiling in cultured fibroblasts
EEG to characterise the epileptic encephalopathy
MRI brain for hypomyelination and cerebral atrophy
Audiological assessment including brainstem-evoked responses for sensorineural loss
Coagulation and endocrine screening as in other type I CDGs
redFlags: Refractory neonatal or infantile seizures with developmental regression
Recurrent hyperthermic episodes without an identifiable infective source
reference.prognosis: The disorder is generally severe; many affected infants have profound neurodevelopmental impairment and shortened survival, although milder cases occur depending on residual enzyme activity.
pitfalls: Overlooking sensorineural hearing loss, which is a useful pointer towards ALG11.
Interpreting the unexplained fever episodes as recurrent infection or sepsis.
Relying on transferrin testing that may be equivocal in the neonatal period.
Grouping all mannosyltransferase CDGs together without lipid-linked oligosaccharide or genetic subtyping.
references: Standard inborn errors of metabolism reference texts
Peer-reviewed reviews of congenital disorders of glycosylation
Clinical genetics and neurometabolic disease references
management: No disease-specific therapy exists; management is supportive and multidisciplinary through a metabolic service
Anticonvulsant therapy for the epileptic encephalopathy, adjusting agents to achieve seizure control
Nutritional and feeding support for failure to thrive, with swallow assessment and enteral feeding as needed
Developmental support with physiotherapy and occupational therapy for central hypotonia and delay
Audiological assessment with hearing aids and rehabilitation for sensorineural hearing loss
Monitor for recurrent unexplained hyperthermia and manage intercurrent illness supportively
Genetic counselling with carrier and prenatal testing for this autosomal recessive disorder
